newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish jet crashes within metres of nuclear ship.
newsitem.headline: Swedish jet crashes within metres of nuclear ship.

text.p: A Swedish air force jet crashed into the Baltic Sea on Wednesday, missing a nuclear-powered Russian warship by only 200 metres (yards), an air force spokesman said.

An AJSH 37 Viggen built by Saab, a surveillance aircraft from the F15 squadron based at Soderhamn in central Sweden, crashed into international waters about 120 kms (75 miles) southeast of the Swedish island of Gotland at 1145 GMT.
Swedish Armed Forces lieutenant colonel Lars Olin said the aircraft hit the water about 200 metres (600 feet) away from a Russian war ship, witnessed by the vessel's crew.
Rescue helicopters were at the scene, but there was no sign of the pilot, only debris from the aircraft's fuselage.
Russia's Itar-Tass news agency identified the Russian warship as the nuclear-powered Russian "Pyotr Veliky".
It said the warship was en route from St Petersburg to the port of Baltiisk in the western Russian enclave of Kaliningrad when the accident occurred.
Russian navy and Swedish officials said the Viggen flew over the ship and crashed when the pilot lost control of the plane as he tried to make a sharp right-hand turn at low altitude.
"It was turning right and losing altitude. It could be due to the horizon. There was 15 km visibility but no horizon...so it's hard to see the altitude," Olin told Reuters.
The Pyotr Veliky and its support ship, the Pylky, were still searching for the pilot and would stay on the scene until Swedish ships arrived, Tass said.
The accident is the third involving Swedish air force Viggens in as many months.
On October 10, two air force JA 37 Viggen jets collided in mid-air over central Sweden. Both pilots ejected, using their parachutes, and were unhurt.
In August, another air force AJS 37 Viggen crashed into the Baltic Sea while on exercises in northern Sweden. The pilot was killed.
